page: Amazon Web Services m6a.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at up to 3.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration allocates 8 virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with two hardware threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides 32.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 3 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without local NVMe or SSD storage volumes, and has no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation reveals strong single-core performance, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2991.08 placing it in the top 25 percent. Multithreaded and general computational tasks fall within the middle tier, with a Geekbench 6 multi-core score of 6267.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 13066.62. Small-block cached read throughput reaches 567.05 GB/sec, while uncached memory bandwidth registers at 37.99 GB/sec for reads and 22.26 GB/sec for writes, both falling into the lower quartile. In application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates consistent throughput across standard server tasks, delivering 9.16 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.74 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. CPU-based medium model (7B) language inference rates remain limited at 8.53 generation tokens per second.

The hardware configuration provides a balanced computational profile for standard cloud workloads where dedicated accelerators and high uncached memory throughput are not required. It is well-fitted for web application hosting, caching tiers, microservices, containerized workloads, continuous integration pipelines, and small to mid-sized relational database environments that rely on external network-attached block storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it delivers a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation. The instance features a 3.6 GHz clock speed, 16 MB of L3 cache, and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no local storage or hardware GPUs. Benchmark metrics demonstrate upper-quartile single-core CPU throughput alongside standard mid-range results across multi-core compute, compression, and Redis operations. Large-block memory bandwidth and CPU-based LLM inference are comparatively restricted. The hardware profile fits general business workloads including container orchestration, backend web services, continuous integration, and standard relational database nodes relying on remote storage.
